findings.title: Shinhan Bank hit by data breach affecting 25,000 customers
findings.summary_md: Shinhan Bank apologized Thursday after a data breach exposed information on about 25,000 customers, and financial regulators launched an urgent inspection. The leaked data included names and phone numbers. This is the first same-day English coverage of the incident, six days before the CrowdStrike post that framed the campaign as AI-driven.

findings.title: (LEAD) Some 25,000 customers' info leaked from Shinhan Bank in apparent hacking
findings.summary_md: Yonhap's lead wire reports personal information of around 25,000 customers leaked from Shinhan Bank via its loan borrowing service, with loan records, annual income, names and phone numbers exposed on September 30. Sources told Yonhap the hackers, suspected to be based overseas, used advanced AI tools, and experts assessed Shinhan was caught in random AI-powered attacks on vulnerable online platforms rather than being specifically targeted. The financial watchdog conducted an on-site inspection.

findings.title: AI Tools Suspected in Korea's Shinhan Bank Hack, Yonhap News Reports
findings.summary_md: Early international pickup of the Yonhap reporting stating that hackers may have had help from AI when they broke into a Shinhan Bank platform and exposed information tied to about 25,000 customers. It notes South Korea's Financial Supervisory Service had begun an emergency on-site inspection to establish the nature and extent of the breach. Published five days before CrowdStrike's analysis of the campaign.

findings.title: ARTEX: A Self-Hosted Autonomous Penetration Testing System Written in Go
findings.summary_md: An independent write-up of the ARTEX project by GitHub user Autumn-27 four days before the campaign attribution: an open-source autonomous penetration testing system pairing a Go backend with a Next.js frontend under AGPL-3.0, winner of Baidu's agent+ attack-defense challenge, with 1,450 stars and 261 forks at the time of writing. It documents approval-gated agent actions, traffic recording, and deployment via Docker or a single binary.

findings.title: Open-Source AI Agent Hacked Seven South Korean Banks, Exposing 65,000 Records
findings.summary_md: Two days before the story's first sighting, TechTimes reported the Financial Security Institute confirmed the ARTEX link after tracing attack IP addresses and server logs from Shinhan Bank, the first institution to report. The key forensic artifact was the string ARTEX-自主渗透测试控制台, roughly autonomous penetration testing console, found in the HTML title of a server used in the campaign. It reported attackers spent up to 43 hours undetected and that the government activated round-the-clock cybersecurity emergency response on October 5.
